title: PrimePar: Efficient Spatial-temporal Tensor Partitioning for Large Transformer Model Training
problem: Existing tensor partitioning systems for LLM training use incomplete partitioning space where sub-operator distribution is limited to spatial dimension, restricting opportunities to avoid collective communication across devices and optimize memory usage during distributed training.
motivation: Training increasingly large transformer-based LLMs requires novel parallel training techniques, and more efficient tensor partitioning can significantly improve both training throughput and memory efficiency.
method: PrimePar splits the training work two ways: across hardware devices (spatial dimension) and across time steps (temporal dimension). By splitting both ways instead of just spatially, it avoids forcing all devices to pause and sync their data, and instead overlaps data transfer between devices with ongoing computation. An optimization algorithm efficiently searches this expanded set of configurations to find the fastest one.
key_novelty: Using both temporal and spatial dimensions for partitioning—instead of just spatial—opens up more ways to divide the work, which reduces inter-device communication overhead and memory usage during training.
contributions: Novel spatial-temporal tensor partitioning primitive extending beyond spatial-only partitioning
Demonstrates communication avoidance opportunities through temporal distribution of sub-operators
Efficient optimization algorithm for finding optimal parallel solutions in spatial-temporal space
Achieves up to 1.68× training throughput improvement with 69% peak memory occupancy reduction

metrics.speedup: 1.68× single-GPU throughput, 1.30× geo-mean speedup at 32 GPUs, 1.46× with 3D parallelism

primary_theme: Spatial-temporal tensor partitioning for efficient LLM training
